The chain establishes the claim exactly: 1.1 gives min_j n_j <= n_i for each i from the defining lower-bound property of the minimum over a finite nonempty index set; 1.2 scales each such inequality by p_i, valid since each p_i is positive and multiplication by a positive real is order-preserving; 1.3 sums the m inequalities termwise and factors the index-independent constant min_j n_j out of the finite sum by distributivity; 1.4 substitutes the hypothesis sum_i p_i = 1 and applies 1*x = x. The endpoint of 1.4, min_{1 <= j <= m} n_j <= sum_{i=1}^m p_i n_i, is syntactically the conclusion asserted here, under the same hypotheses (p_i positive reals summing to 1, n_i real), so node 1 requires no further inference beyond discharging into 1.4. Every hypothesis is used legitimately and none is smuggled in: positivity enters only at 1.2, normalization only at 1.4, finiteness and nonemptiness of {1, ..., m} only at 1.1 and 1.3. No step divides, changes sign, or reorders quantifiers, and the argument is sound for arbitrary real n_i including negative values.
